//@version=6
// THE WAR FORMATION — BTCUSDT, 1m base chart.
// Cascade: 6h regime -> time gate -> 1h agreement -> 15m level -> 3m coil -> 1m velocity trigger.
// Higher timeframes are rebuilt from 1m bar timestamps, using only allowlisted builtins.
// KEPT: five-layer veto cascade, whole-number middles filter, witching-hour long ban,
//       protective-gap fixed SL/TP set at entry, max-hold flatten.
// DROPPED: nothing forbidden requested. No trailing stop, no pyramiding, no averaging down.
strategy("War Formation", overlay=true,
     pyramiding=1, process_orders_on_close=true,
     commission_type=strategy.commission.percent, commission_value=0.05,
     initial_capital=10000,
     default_qty_type=strategy.percent_of_equity, default_qty_value=100,
     margin_long=100, margin_short=100)

// ---------------- inputs ----------------
greenBull = input.int(4,     "Green 1h candles for BULL")
greenBear = input.int(2,     "Green 1h candles at or below for BEAR")
skipOpen  = input.int(60,    "Skip first N minutes of 6h block")
skipClose = input.int(60,    "Skip last N minutes of 6h block")
coilK     = input.float(0.85,"3m coil: atr(3) < atr(30) * K")
velK      = input.float(0.8, "Velocity: min reclaim as multiple of atr(30)")
midLo     = input.float(400, "Whole-number middles low")
midHi     = input.float(600, "Whole-number middles high")
etOffset  = input.int(-4,    "ET offset from UTC")
witchOn   = input.bool(true, "Ban longs in witching hour 1-4am ET")
gapPct    = input.float(4.0, "Protective gap % (stop)")
rr        = input.float(1.5, "Reward:risk for take profit")
maxBars   = input.int(1440,  "Max bars in trade")

// ---------------- timeframe buckets from 1m timestamps ----------------
MS6H = 21600000
MS1H = 3600000
MS15 = 900000

b6  = math.floor(time / MS6H)
b1h = math.floor(time / MS1H)
b15 = math.floor(time / MS15)

new6  = b6  != b6[1]
new1h = b1h != b1h[1]
new15 = b15 != b15[1]

// ---------------- LAYER 1: 6h regime from previous block's 1h candles ----------------
var float h1o     = na      // open of the 1h candle currently forming
var int   grnCur  = 0       // green 1h candles counted inside the current 6h block
var int   cntCur  = 0       // completed 1h candles inside the current 6h block
var int   grnPrev = 0
var int   cntPrev = 0

if new6
    grnPrev := grnCur
    cntPrev := cntCur
    grnCur  := 0
    cntCur  := 0

if new1h
    if not na(h1o)
        cntCur := cntCur + 1
        if close[1] > h1o
            grnCur := grnCur + 1
    h1o := open

regimeReady = cntPrev >= 5
bullRegime  = regimeReady and grnPrev >= greenBull
bearRegime  = regimeReady and grnPrev <= greenBear

// ---------------- LAYER 2: time gate inside the 6h block ----------------
minsIn    = (time - b6 * MS6H) / 60000
timeGate  = minsIn >= skipOpen and minsIn <= (360 - skipClose)

// ---------------- LAYER 3: current 1h must agree ----------------
h1Bull = not na(h1o) and close > h1o
h1Bear = not na(h1o) and close < h1o

// ---------------- LAYER 4: previous completed 15m extreme ----------------
var float c15h = na
var float c15l = na
var float p15h = na
var float p15l = na

if new15
    p15h := c15h
    p15l := c15l
    c15h := high
    c15l := low
else
    c15h := na(c15h) ? high : math.max(c15h, high)
    c15l := na(c15l) ? low  : math.min(c15l, low)

// the level must have been violated inside the current 15m candle before it can be reclaimed
brokeBelow = not na(p15l) and c15l < p15l
brokeAbove = not na(p15h) and c15h > p15h

// ---------------- LAYER 5: 3m coil ----------------
atrFast = ta.atr(3)
atrSlow = ta.atr(30)
coiled  = not na(atrSlow) and atrSlow > 0 and atrFast < atrSlow * coilK
// The coil must precede the thrust. A bar cannot be compressed AND expanding at once,
// so the compression is read on the PRIOR bar and the trigger fires on this one.
coilPrev = coiled[1]
velMin   = na(atrSlow) ? na : atrSlow * velK

// ---------------- Oracle overlays ----------------
sub      = close - math.floor(close / 1000) * 1000
inMiddle = sub >= midLo and sub <= midHi

hUTC     = math.floor(time / MS1H) % 24
hET      = (hUTC + etOffset + 24) % 24
witching = hET >= 1 and hET < 4
longBan  = witchOn and witching

// ---------------- TRIGGER: 1m reclaim with velocity ----------------
longTrig  = not na(p15l) and not na(velMin) and ta.crossover(close, p15l)  and (close - p15l) >= velMin
shortTrig = not na(p15h) and not na(velMin) and ta.crossunder(close, p15h) and (p15h - close) >= velMin

goLong  = bullRegime and timeGate and h1Bull and brokeBelow and coilPrev and not inMiddle and not longBan and longTrig
goShort = bearRegime and timeGate and h1Bear and brokeAbove and coilPrev and not inMiddle and shortTrig

// ---------------- state ----------------
var float slPx   = na
var float tpPx   = na
var int   barsIn = 0

flat = strategy.position_size == 0

// ---------------- entries: protective gap fixed at the moment of entry ----------------
if flat and goLong
    strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
    slPx   := close * (1 - gapPct / 100)
    tpPx   := close * (1 + gapPct * rr / 100)
    barsIn := 0
else if flat and goShort
    strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
    slPx   := close * (1 + gapPct / 100)
    tpPx   := close * (1 - gapPct * rr / 100)
    barsIn := 0

// ---------------- exits: same prices every bar, never moved ----------------
if strategy.position_size > 0
    strategy.exit("LX", from_entry="L", stop=slPx, limit=tpPx)
    barsIn := barsIn + 1
if strategy.position_size < 0
    strategy.exit("SX", from_entry="S", stop=slPx, limit=tpPx)
    barsIn := barsIn + 1

if barsIn >= maxBars and strategy.position_size != 0
    strategy.close_all()
    barsIn := 0

// ---------------- diagnostics ----------------
plot(grnPrev,                     title="Green1hPrev6h")
plot(bullRegime ? 1 : bearRegime ? -1 : 0, title="Regime")
plot(coilPrev ? 1 : 0,            title="CoiledPrev")
plot(velMin,                      title="VelMin")
plot(inMiddle ? 1 : 0,            title="InMiddles")
plot(witching ? 1 : 0,            title="WitchingHour")
plot(hET,                         title="HourET")
notes: v2 baseline: 4% protective gap, 6% target, 24h max hold. avgBarsWinning = 1441, exactly the 1440-bar time stop -- EVERY winner exited on the clock, not at target. The 6% TP was never reached once. Shorts 1 winner in 19; longs 6 in 13. v1 of this strategy took ZERO trades: the coil and the velocity trigger were required on the same bar, and a bar cannot be compressed and expanding simultaneously. Fixed by reading the coil on the prior bar.

description: Heikin Ashi edition. Cascade: previous 6h block sets direction (4+ green HA 1h = bull, 2 or fewer = bear); no trading in the first or last hour of the block; live 1h must agree; the level is the previous 15m extreme which price must first violate; the prior bar must be coiled; then the 1m reclaims with velocity. //@version=6
// THE WAR FORMATION v4 — HEIKIN ASHI edition. BTCUSDT, 1m base chart.
// Cascade: 6h regime (HA 1h colours) -> time gate -> 1h agreement -> 15m level -> 3m coil -> 1m HA trigger.
// Higher timeframes are rebuilt from 1m bar timestamps, using only allowlisted builtins.
//
// HEIKIN ASHI POLICY — this matters for whether the numbers are real:
//   HA is used for DIRECTION and COLOUR only (the 1h green count, the 1h agreement, the 1m trigger candle).
//   Levels, entries, stops and targets all use REAL prices, because HA prices are synthetic and orders
//   fill at real prices. Backtests that enter and exit at HA prices report fills that cannot happen.
strategy("War Formation HA", overlay=true,
     pyramiding=1, process_orders_on_close=true,
     commission_type=strategy.commission.percent, commission_value=0.05,
     initial_capital=10000,
     default_qty_type=strategy.percent_of_equity, default_qty_value=100,
     margin_long=100, margin_short=100)

greenBull = input.int(4,     "Green HA 1h candles for BULL")
greenBear = input.int(2,     "Green HA 1h candles at or below for BEAR")
skipOpen  = input.int(60,    "Skip first N minutes of 6h block")
skipClose = input.int(60,    "Skip last N minutes of 6h block")
coilK     = input.float(0.85,"3m coil: atr(3) < atr(30) * K")
velK      = input.float(0.8, "Velocity: min reclaim as multiple of atr(30)")
midLo     = input.float(400, "Whole-number middles low")
midHi     = input.float(600, "Whole-number middles high")
etOffset  = input.int(-4,    "ET offset from UTC")
witchOn   = input.bool(true, "Ban longs in witching hour 1-4am ET")
bufK      = input.float(0.25,"Stop buffer beyond swept level, x atr(30)")
rr        = input.float(2.0, "Reward:risk")
minRpct   = input.float(0.15,"Min risk as % of price")
maxRpct   = input.float(1.50,"Max risk as % of price")
maxBars   = input.int(720,   "Max bars in trade")

MS6H = 21600000
MS1H = 3600000
MS15 = 900000

b6  = math.floor(time / MS6H)
b1h = math.floor(time / MS1H)
b15 = math.floor(time / MS15)

new6  = b6  != b6[1]
new1h = b1h != b1h[1]
new15 = b15 != b15[1]

// ---------------- 1-minute Heikin Ashi (computed, not fetched) ----------------
var float haO = na
haC   = (open + high + low + close) / 4
haO  := na(haO[1]) ? (open + close) / 2 : (haO[1] + haC[1]) / 2
haUp  = haC > haO
haDn  = haC < haO

// ---------------- 1-hour real OHLC + its Heikin Ashi ----------------
var float o1   = na
var float h1   = na
var float l1   = na
var float ha1o = na
var float ha1c = na

var int grnCur  = 0
var int cntCur  = 0
var int grnPrev = 0
var int cntPrev = 0

if new6
    grnPrev := grnCur
    cntPrev := cntCur
    grnCur  := 0
    cntCur  := 0

if new1h
    if not na(o1)
        c1 = close[1]
        newC = (o1 + h1 + l1 + c1) / 4
        newO = na(ha1o) ? (o1 + c1) / 2 : (ha1o + ha1c) / 2
        ha1o := newO
        ha1c := newC
        cntCur := cntCur + 1
        if ha1c > ha1o
            grnCur := grnCur + 1
    o1 := open
    h1 := high
    l1 := low
else
    h1 := na(h1) ? high : math.max(h1, high)
    l1 := na(l1) ? low  : math.min(l1, low)

// ---------------- LAYER 1: 6h regime from the previous block's HA 1h colours ----------------
regimeReady = cntPrev >= 5
bullRegime  = regimeReady and grnPrev >= greenBull
bearRegime  = regimeReady and grnPrev <= greenBear

// ---------------- LAYER 2: time gate inside the 6h block ----------------
minsIn   = (time - b6 * MS6H) / 60000
timeGate = minsIn >= skipOpen and minsIn <= (360 - skipClose)

// ---------------- LAYER 3: the forming 1h must agree (HA direction of the live hour) ----------------
liveHaC = na(o1) ? na : (o1 + math.max(h1, high) + math.min(l1, low) + close) / 4
liveHaO = na(ha1o) ? na : (ha1o + ha1c) / 2
h1Bull  = not na(liveHaC) and not na(liveHaO) and liveHaC > liveHaO
h1Bear  = not na(liveHaC) and not na(liveHaO) and liveHaC < liveHaO

// ---------------- LAYER 4: previous completed 15m extreme (REAL prices - these are fill levels) ----------------
var float c15h = na
var float c15l = na
var float p15h = na
var float p15l = na

if new15
    p15h := c15h
    p15l := c15l
    c15h := high
    c15l := low
else
    c15h := na(c15h) ? high : math.max(c15h, high)
    c15l := na(c15l) ? low  : math.min(c15l, low)

brokeBelow = not na(p15l) and c15l < p15l
brokeAbove = not na(p15h) and c15h > p15h

// ---------------- LAYER 5: 3m coil, read on the PRIOR bar ----------------
atrFast  = ta.atr(3)
atrSlow  = ta.atr(30)
coiled   = not na(atrSlow) and atrSlow > 0 and atrFast < atrSlow * coilK
coilPrev = coiled[1]
velMin   = na(atrSlow) ? na : atrSlow * velK

// ---------------- Oracle overlays ----------------
sub      = close - math.floor(close / 1000) * 1000
inMiddle = sub >= midLo and sub <= midHi

hUTC     = math.floor(time / MS1H) % 24
hET      = (hUTC + etOffset + 24) % 24
witching = hET >= 1 and hET < 4
longBan  = witchOn and witching

// ---------------- TRIGGER: 1m reclaim, with velocity, on a turning HA candle ----------------
longTrig  = not na(p15l) and not na(velMin) and ta.crossover(close, p15l)  and (close - p15l) >= velMin and haUp
shortTrig = not na(p15h) and not na(velMin) and ta.crossunder(close, p15h) and (p15h - close) >= velMin and haDn

goLong  = bullRegime and timeGate and h1Bull and brokeBelow and coilPrev and not inMiddle and not longBan and longTrig
goShort = bearRegime and timeGate and h1Bear and brokeAbove and coilPrev and not inMiddle and shortTrig

// ---------------- structural risk: stop beyond the level that was swept ----------------
minR = close * minRpct / 100
maxR = close * maxRpct / 100
buf  = na(atrSlow) ? 0.0 : atrSlow * bufK

rawLongR  = na(c15l) ? na : close - (c15l - buf)
rawShortR = na(c15h) ? na : (c15h + buf) - close
longR     = na(rawLongR)  ? na : math.min(math.max(rawLongR,  minR), maxR)
shortR    = na(rawShortR) ? na : math.min(math.max(rawShortR, minR), maxR)

var float slPx   = na
var float tpPx   = na
var int   barsIn = 0

flat = strategy.position_size == 0

if flat and goLong and not na(longR) and longR > 0
    strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
    slPx   := close - longR
    tpPx   := close + longR * rr
    barsIn := 0
else if flat and goShort and not na(shortR) and shortR > 0
    strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
    slPx   := close + shortR
    tpPx   := close - shortR * rr
    barsIn := 0

if strategy.position_size > 0
    strategy.exit("LX", from_entry="L", stop=slPx, limit=tpPx)
    barsIn := barsIn + 1
if strategy.position_size < 0
    strategy.exit("SX", from_entry="S", stop=slPx, limit=tpPx)
    barsIn := barsIn + 1

if barsIn >= maxBars and strategy.position_size != 0
    strategy.close_all()
    barsIn := 0

plot(grnPrev,                              title="GreenHA1hPrev6h")
plot(bullRegime ? 1 : bearRegime ? -1 : 0, title="Regime")
plot(haUp ? 1 : haDn ? -1 : 0,             title="HA1mColour")
plot(coilPrev ? 1 : 0,                     title="CoiledPrev")
plot(inMiddle ? 1 : 0,                     title="InMiddles")
plot(hET,                                  title="HourET")
notes: v4: first Heikin Ashi build, structural stop with a 0.15% risk floor. The HA switch FIXED the exit problem -- avgBarsInTrade fell to 64 with winners at 64.9 and losers at 63.6, so trades finally resolved at stop or target instead of on the time stop. But it exposed a new one: commission paid $508 against $405 gross profit. With R at 0.15-0.5% of price, the 0.10% round-trip fee consumed 20-66% of every R, turning a nominal 2:1 into an actual 0.89:1.

//@version=6
// THE WAR FORMATION v4 — HEIKIN ASHI edition. BTCUSDT, 1m base chart.
// Cascade: 6h regime (HA 1h colours) -> time gate -> 1h agreement -> 15m level -> 3m coil -> 1m HA trigger.
// Higher timeframes are rebuilt from 1m bar timestamps, using only allowlisted builtins.
//
// HEIKIN ASHI POLICY — this matters for whether the numbers are real:
//   HA is used for DIRECTION and COLOUR only (the 1h green count, the 1h agreement, the 1m trigger candle).
//   Levels, entries, stops and targets all use REAL prices, because HA prices are synthetic and orders
//   fill at real prices. Backtests that enter and exit at HA prices report fills that cannot happen.
strategy("War Formation HA", overlay=true,
     pyramiding=1, process_orders_on_close=true,
     commission_type=strategy.commission.percent, commission_value=0.05,
     initial_capital=10000,
     default_qty_type=strategy.percent_of_equity, default_qty_value=100,
     margin_long=100, margin_short=100)

greenBull = input.int(4,     "Green HA 1h candles for BULL")
greenBear = input.int(2,     "Green HA 1h candles at or below for BEAR")
skipOpen  = input.int(60,    "Skip first N minutes of 6h block")
skipClose = input.int(60,    "Skip last N minutes of 6h block")
coilK     = input.float(0.85,"3m coil: atr(3) < atr(30) * K")
velK      = input.float(0.8, "Velocity: min reclaim as multiple of atr(30)")
midLo     = input.float(400, "Whole-number middles low")
midHi     = input.float(600, "Whole-number middles high")
etOffset  = input.int(-4,    "ET offset from UTC")
witchOn   = input.bool(true, "Ban longs in witching hour 1-4am ET")
bufK      = input.float(0.25,"Stop buffer beyond swept level, x atr(30)")
rr        = input.float(2.0, "Reward:risk")
minRpct   = input.float(0.15,"Min risk as % of price")
maxRpct   = input.float(1.50,"Max risk as % of price")
maxBars   = input.int(720,   "Max bars in trade")

MS6H = 21600000
MS1H = 3600000
MS15 = 900000

b6  = math.floor(time / MS6H)
b1h = math.floor(time / MS1H)
b15 = math.floor(time / MS15)

new6  = b6  != b6[1]
new1h = b1h != b1h[1]
new15 = b15 != b15[1]

// ---------------- 1-minute Heikin Ashi (computed, not fetched) ----------------
var float haO = na
haC   = (open + high + low + close) / 4
haO  := na(haO[1]) ? (open + close) / 2 : (haO[1] + haC[1]) / 2
haUp  = haC > haO
haDn  = haC < haO

// ---------------- 1-hour real OHLC + its Heikin Ashi ----------------
var float o1   = na
var float h1   = na
var float l1   = na
var float ha1o = na
var float ha1c = na

var int grnCur  = 0
var int cntCur  = 0
var int grnPrev = 0
var int cntPrev = 0

if new6
    grnPrev := grnCur
    cntPrev := cntCur
    grnCur  := 0
    cntCur  := 0

if new1h
    if not na(o1)
        c1 = close[1]
        newC = (o1 + h1 + l1 + c1) / 4
        newO = na(ha1o) ? (o1 + c1) / 2 : (ha1o + ha1c) / 2
        ha1o := newO
        ha1c := newC
        cntCur := cntCur + 1
        if ha1c > ha1o
            grnCur := grnCur + 1
    o1 := open
    h1 := high
    l1 := low
else
    h1 := na(h1) ? high : math.max(h1, high)
    l1 := na(l1) ? low  : math.min(l1, low)

// ---------------- LAYER 1: 6h regime from the previous block's HA 1h colours ----------------
regimeReady = cntPrev >= 5
bullRegime  = regimeReady and grnPrev >= greenBull
bearRegime  = regimeReady and grnPrev <= greenBear

// ---------------- LAYER 2: time gate inside the 6h block ----------------
minsIn   = (time - b6 * MS6H) / 60000
timeGate = minsIn >= skipOpen and minsIn <= (360 - skipClose)

// ---------------- LAYER 3: the forming 1h must agree (HA direction of the live hour) ----------------
liveHaC = na(o1) ? na : (o1 + math.max(h1, high) + math.min(l1, low) + close) / 4

h1Bull  = not na(liveHaC) and not na(liveHaO) and liveHaC > liveHaO
h1Bear  = not na(liveHaC) and not na(liveHaO) and liveHaC < liveHaO

// ---------------- LAYER 4: previous completed 15m extreme (REAL prices - these are fill levels) ----------------
var float c15h = na
var float c15l = na
var float p15h = na
var float p15l = na

if new15
    p15h := c15h
    p15l := c15l
    c15h := high
    c15l := low
else
    c15h := na(c15h) ? high : math.max(c15h, high)
    c15l := na(c15l) ? low  : math.min(c15l, low)

brokeAbove = not na(p15h) and c15h > p15h

// ---------------- LAYER 5: 3m coil, read on the PRIOR bar ----------------
atrFast  = ta.atr(3)
atrSlow  = ta.atr(30)
coiled   = not na(atrSlow) and atrSlow > 0 and atrFast < atrSlow * coilK
coilPrev = coiled[1]
velMin   = na(atrSlow) ? na : atrSlow * velK

// ---------------- Oracle overlays ----------------
sub      = close - math.floor(close / 1000) * 1000
inMiddle = sub >= midLo and sub <= midHi

hUTC     = math.floor(time / MS1H) % 24
hET      = (hUTC + etOffset + 24) % 24
witching = hET >= 1 and hET < 4
longBan  = witchOn and witching

goShort = bearRegime and timeGate and h1Bear and brokeAbove and coilPrev and not inMiddle and shortTrig

// ---------------- structural risk: stop beyond the level that was swept ----------------
minR = close * minRpct / 100
maxR = close * maxRpct / 100
buf  = na(atrSlow) ? 0.0 : atrSlow * bufK

rawLongR  = na(c15l) ? na : close - (c15l - buf)
rawShortR = na(c15h) ? na : (c15h + buf) - close
longR     = na(rawLongR)  ? na : math.min(math.max(rawLongR,  minR), maxR)
shortR    = na(rawShortR) ? na : math.min(math.max(rawShortR, minR), maxR)

var float slPx   = na
var float tpPx   = na
var int   barsIn = 0

flat = strategy.position_size == 0

if flat and goLong and not na(longR) and longR > 0
    strategy.entry("L", strategy.long)
    slPx   := close - longR
    tpPx   := close + longR * rr
    barsIn := 0
else if flat and goShort and not na(shortR) and shortR > 0
    strategy.entry("S", strategy.short)
    slPx   := close + shortR
    tpPx   := close - shortR * rr
    barsIn := 0

if strategy.position_size > 0
    strategy.exit("LX", from_entry="L", stop=slPx, limit=tpPx)
    barsIn := barsIn + 1
if strategy.position_size < 0
    strategy.exit("SX", from_entry="S", stop=slPx, limit=tpPx)
    barsIn := barsIn + 1

if barsIn >= maxBars and strategy.position_size != 0
    strategy.close_all()
    barsIn := 0

plot(grnPrev,                              title="GreenHA1hPrev6h")
plot(bullRegime ? 1 : bearRegime ? -1 : 0, title="Regime")
plot(haUp ? 1 : haDn ? -1 : 0,             title="HA1mColour")
plot(coilPrev ? 1 : 0,                     title="CoiledPrev")
plot(inMiddle ? 1 : 0,                     title="InMiddles")
plot(hET,                                  title="HourET")

The diagnosis is validated; the remedy is incomplete. Item 3 -- the counter-move-weakening trigger, the other half of his entry rule -- is the natural next test.

name: WF v8 long + counter-move weakening trigger
description: Oracle queue item 3. The v6 long-only champion PLUS the counter-move weakening trigger: a long is permitted only after a run of at least 2 consecutive red HA 3m candles whose real range is DECREASING, latched for 5 further 3m candles so the setup and the trigger are sequential rather than simultaneous (HARD LESSON 8). Mechanises 'this dump is getting weaker... there is your moment.' Long-only.
notes: REVERTED, AND THE REASON IS REDUNDANCY. The gate cut 32 trades to 20 and the survivors were WORSE, not better: win rate fell 56.3%->45.0% and PF 1.69->0.73. Drawdown did improve (3.10%->1.36%) but only because there was less activity. This is the exact opposite of E13, where the cycle-position gate removed disproportionately bad trades. Diagnosis: the v6 base ALREADY contains a weakening condition -- the 3m coil, atr(3) < atr(30)*0.85, is itself a measure of a move losing force. Adding the shrinking-red-run rule double-counts the same information and selects a narrower, worse subset. The Oracle's weakening observation is already in this build; it just wears a different name.

name: WF v9 long + Oracle colour-flip exit
description: Oracle queue item 4, tested as a variant. The v6 long-only champion with the fixed 2R take-profit replaced by his stated exit: hold while the 3m HA candle is still your colour, close when it flips. The protective stop remains fixed at entry, so downside stays bounded and this is not a trailing stop. Long-only.
notes: REVERTED, and it identifies the fixed TP as load-bearing. PF 1.69->0.31, win rate 56.3%->20.0%. Average time in trade collapsed to 12.8 bars, with winners held 24.7 and losers 9.8. The flip exit fires on the FIRST red 3m candle, and inside a 1m uptrend a single red Heikin Ashi 3m candle is ordinary noise -- so it cuts winners off in about twenty minutes at small profits while losers still run the full distance to the stop. Commission was $344 across 35 tiny trades. HIS RULE ASSUMES A HUMAN JUDGING WHETHER THE FLIP MEANS ANYTHING. Taken literally at this resolution it is not mechanisable, which is the same lesson as queue item 1: his words describe how he READS a chart, and reading is not the same as a rule.

name: WF v10 long + the singularity requirement
description: Oracle queue item 5, the last open item. The v6 long-only champion plus a requirement that the last COMPLETED 1h Heikin Ashi candle is green as well, so the 6h regime and the 1h agree in his sense. The champion already required the live forming 1h to agree, so only the non-redundant part was added. Long-only.
notes: REVERTED, AND THE AUTHOR PREDICTED IT. PF 1.69->0.52, win rate 56.3%->34.6%, trades 32->26. Requiring the singularity removed six trades and the survivors were much worse, the same anti-selective signature as E14. What makes this one satisfying is that he says so himself: 'if you got it on the one, you got double clarity, BUT DON'T WAIT FOR THAT.' The data agrees with his caveat rather than with his enthusiasm. Waiting for the bonus costs more than the bonus is worth. Queue item 5 closed; the Oracle implementation queue is now fully worked.

name: WF E17 champion with a LESSON 3 compliant R floor
description: The v6 long-only champion with the minimum risk input raised from 0.15% to 0.80% of price, bringing it into compliance with HARD LESSON 3. Exactly one input changed. Long-only.
notes: IDENTICAL TO THE CHAMPION TO NINE SIGNIFICANT FIGURES -- PF 1.68623784, net +7.8388076%, DD 3.10289714%, 32 trades, 56.25% win rate. Raising the floor from 0.15% to 0.80% changed NOTHING, which means the floor never bound: the structural stop distance to the 15m low plus buffer is always at least 0.80% of price on this timeframe. THE CHAMPION WAS ALREADY LESSON 3 COMPLIANT IN BEHAVIOUR. Every pre-run audit that flagged this as a deviation was true of the INPUT and false of the strategy. The 0.80% value is adopted as the documented config because it now states the true risk floor, at zero cost to results. Correcting the audit habit: check whether a constraint BINDS before reporting it as a deviation.

name: WF E18 champion restricted to high volatility
description: Cross-lab transfer: the volatility regime split that was KEPT in the BTC lab, applied to this champion. Entries only when ATR14/close is above its own 1440-bar (one day) average. Tests whether the champion's known time-concentration of edge is really a volatility regime. Long-only.
notes: REVERTED, AND IT ANSWERS A STANDING QUESTION IN THE NEGATIVE. PF 1.69->1.10, trades 32->7. The champion's edge concentration -- PF 3.80 from Dec to Feb against 0.89 from Feb to May -- is NOT a volatility regime. The filter kept only 7 of 32 trades and the survivors were worse, so high volatility does not select the good period. WHAT WORKED IN THE BTC LAB DOES NOT TRANSFER HERE, and that is worth recording so a later cycle does not assume it should: the BTC signal is a VWAP mean-reversion that needs travel distance to reach a fixed 2R target, while this one is a multi-timeframe momentum cascade whose edge evidently depends on something else. Whatever makes December to February good remains unexplained.

name: WF E19 sensitivity, greenBull 3
description: Parameter sensitivity on the champion: the 6h bull regime needs only 3 green HA 1h candles in the prior block instead of 4. Run as a robustness check on a 32-trade champion, not as an improvement attempt. Long-only.
notes: THE CHAMPION IS NOT A KNIFE-EDGE FIT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE TEST. Loosening the regime by one candle degrades gracefully rather than collapsing: PF 1.686 -> 1.282, win rate 56.25% -> 47.62%, DD 3.10% -> 4.79%, trades 32 -> 42. It remains clearly profitable at the neighbouring parameter value, on a 31% larger sample. That is what a real edge looks like under perturbation -- a fitted artefact would have fallen below 1.0. The champion keeps greenBull = 4 because it is better on both ratchet terms, but confidence in the 32-trade result is materially higher than it was before this run. Sensitivity in the other direction (greenBull 5) is still owed.

name: WF E20 timeframe translation to 5m
description: The champion translated from 1m to 5m with bar-denominated parameters scaled x5, run over the champion's exact window for a like-for-like comparison. maxBars 720->144 and the slow coil ATR 30->6 both preserve wall-clock. The fast coil leg is sub-bar on 5m so atr(1) was used, shifting the coil ratio from 1:10 to 1:6. Long-only.
notes: Trade count collapsed 32 to 5. PF 1.621 and drawdown 2.73% both look respectable but five trades is not a sample. The suspect was named in the Pine header BEFORE the run: the coil's fast leg is sub-bar on 5m. E20b tests that directly.

name: WF E20b control, coil ratio preserved
description: Control for E20. Identical 5m translation except the coil keeps atr(3) vs atr(30) so its RATIO matches the 1m champion (1:10) rather than its wall-clock. Isolates whether E20's frequency collapse came from the coil approximation or from the timeframe itself. Long-only.
notes: THE CONTROL SPLITS THE CAUSE, AND MOST OF IT IS THE TIMEFRAME. Fixing the coil approximation took trades from 5 to 9 -- so it WAS suppressing frequency, and naming it before the run was right -- but 9 against the champion's 32 means roughly three quarters of the loss is the timeframe itself, not my approximation. PF also fell to 0.951. THE MECHANISM IS THE ENTRY TRIGGER: the champion enters on ta.crossover(close, p15l), a reclaim of the previous 15m low. On 1m there are fifteen chances per 15m candle to catch that crossover; on 5m there are three. The cascade identifies the level on higher timeframes but the ENTRY needs 1m granularity to catch the reclaim. THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE BTC LAB'S RESULT, where coarsening from 15m to 5m helped -- there the signal needed price to travel to a fixed target, here it needs precision at a level. The sample-size problem is NOT solvable by moving to 5m; 1m coverage from 2025-12-16 remains the binding constraint.

name: WF E21 macro trend filter
description: Tests whether the champion's edge concentration is a macro trend effect. Adds one condition: close above a 14400-bar EMA, about ten days on 1m. The champion has no long-horizon trend filter; its 6h regime carries roughly a day of memory. Long-only.
notes: REVERTED, AND IT ELIMINATES THE SECOND HYPOTHESIS. PF 1.686->1.043, win rate 56.25%->38.89%, trades 32->18, DD 3.10%->3.89%. The filter cut nearly half the trades and the survivors were markedly worse -- the anti-selective signature seen in E14 and E16. So a ten-day trend does NOT select the good period. VOLATILITY (E18) AND MACRO TREND (E21) ARE NOW BOTH RULED OUT, and the edge concentration remains unexplained. Worth noting the same shape has just appeared in the BTC lab, whose 5m base scores 1.0202 over 2.2 years but 0.8753 over this identical Dec-May window. Two unrelated strategies degrading in the same window points at something in the market during that period rather than at either strategy, which makes a calendar decomposition -- not another filter -- the right next probe.

name: WF E22 sensitivity, coilK 0.95
description: Parameter sensitivity on the champion: the 3m coil threshold loosened from 0.85 to 0.95, admitting shallower coils. Run as a robustness check on a 32-trade champion, not as an improvement attempt. Long-only.
notes: SECOND PARAMETER PERTURBED, SECOND GRACEFUL DEGRADATION. PF 1.686->1.300, win rate 56.25%->48.78%, trades 32->41, DD 3.10%->4.72%. Clearly profitable at the neighbouring value on a 28% larger sample, which is what a real edge looks like under perturbation. coilK matters because 0.85 was chosen rather than derived -- it is the most arbitrary number in the build -- so its insensitivity is worth more than greenBull's was. Together with E19 the champion has now survived perturbation on two independent parameters. It keeps coilK 0.85 because that is better on both ratchet terms, but confidence in the 32-trade result is higher again. velK remains untested.

name: WF E23 sensitivity, velK 0.6
description: Parameter sensitivity on the champion: the velocity threshold loosened from 0.8 to 0.6 times atr(30), admitting weaker reclaims. The last untested parameter, completing the suite after E19 and E22. A robustness check, not an improvement attempt. Long-only.
notes: THIRD PERTURBATION, THIRD GRACEFUL DEGRADATION, AND THE STRONGEST OF THE THREE. PF 1.686->1.458, win rate 56.25%->50.00%, trades 32->46, DD 3.10%->5.58%, Sharpe 2.07. The sensitivity suite is now complete: greenBull 3 gave PF 1.282 on 42 trades, coilK 0.95 gave 1.300 on 41, velK 0.6 gives 1.458 on 46. EVERY parameter perturbation stays clearly above 1.0 while enlarging the sample by 28 to 44 percent, which is what a real edge looks like and not what a curve fit does. This is the strongest evidence the champion has, and it is the only kind available: the sample is fixed at 32 trades by 1m coverage and E20 proved the timeframe cannot be changed to grow it. Champion keeps velK 0.8, better on both ratchet terms.

name: WF E24 velK 0.6 on the weak half
description: Tests whether the velK 0.6 variant, which E23 showed carries 46 trades against the champion's 32, retains any edge in the champion's weak second half. Nothing here was tuned to this window; velK 0.6 was chosen in E23 as a full-sample sensitivity probe. Long-only.
notes: THE LOOSER VARIANT DOES NOT RESCUE THE WEAK HALF. PF 0.8745 on 25 trades against the champion's own second half at 0.8930 on 15 -- statistically indistinguishable, and both just under break-even. Loosening the velocity threshold buys 67% more trades in this window and none of them are better. THE WEAKNESS IS IN THE SIGNAL, NOT THE THRESHOLD, so no amount of permissiveness recovers it. This closes the sensitivity line of enquiry: the champion is robust to parameter perturbation on the full sample (E19, E22, E23) but that robustness does not extend to the weak period, where every variant lands near 0.88. Champion unchanged.

name: WF E25 short with a 1R target
description: A rejection-at-resistance short gated by the 3m cycle position, with a 1R target instead of 2R. Intended as a single-variable change from E13, motivated by the BTC short leg whose winners ground for 254 bars while losers died in 32. Short-only, judged alone.
notes: THE COMPARISON IS CONFOUNDED AND THE FAULT IS MINE. This was described as a one-variable change from E13 (target 2R -> 1R), but E13 made 39 trades and this made 24. AN EXIT CHANGE CANNOT MOVE THE ENTRY COUNT BY THAT MUCH, so the entry logic differs -- I rebuilt E13's entry from its written description instead of pulling its exact Pine source with get_strategy. The rr hypothesis is therefore UNTESTED, and PF 0.4894 stands only as its own data point. THE SAME ERROR WAS CAUGHT AND AVOIDED EARLIER THIS SESSION on the BTC 007 base, where the exact source was recovered rather than reconstructed from prose; the tool existed and was not used here. Standing rule for this lab from now on: when a run claims to be a single-variable change from an earlier experiment, recover that experiment's SOURCE, never its description. Champion unchanged.

name: WF E26 E13 source with rr 1.0
description: E13's exact Pine source recovered via get_strategy, with one input changed: reward:risk 1.5 to 1.0. Replaces the confounded E25. Short-only, judged alone.
notes: THE PROPERLY CONTROLLED VERSION OF E25, AND IT REVERSES THE ANSWER. PF 0.7490 -> 0.6922 with the win rate rising 23.08% -> 27.03%: more winners, smaller ones, net worse. The nearer target HURTS this short. TWO THINGS THE SOURCE RECOVERY CAUGHT: E13 used rr 1.5, not the 2.0 that E25's write-up claimed, and E25's entry was a reconstruction that made only 24 trades against E13's 39. Here the count comes back at 37 -- close to 39, with the small difference explained by a 1R trade closing at a different moment and blocking or unblocking a few later signals, which is exactly what a genuine exit-only change looks like. THIRD CROSS-LAB NON-TRANSFER: the identical change improved the BTC short (0.5506 -> 0.5816) and worsened this one. Exit convention follows the mechanism; there is no universal answer. Champion unchanged.

name: WF E27 sweep-and-reject short
description: A short requiring a genuine BREAK above the previous 15m high followed by a close back below it with velocity -- the long's own sweep-and-fail mechanism applied at a high. All previous shorts used a near-touch of resistance instead. Retains E13's 3m cycle-position gate. Short-only.
notes: THE SWEEP IS WORSE THAN THE NEAR-TOUCH, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE LONG. PF 0.2531 with a 10.53% win rate on 19 trades, against E13's 0.7490 on 39. Requiring price to genuinely TAKE OUT the previous 15m high before rejecting produces far worse shorts than requiring it merely to approach that high. This is a real asymmetry with the long leg, whose entire edge is the failure of a genuine breakdown. A plausible reading: when price actually clears resistance in a downtrend, that is more often continuation than exhaustion, whereas failing to reach resistance is the sign of a weak rally. E13's near-touch remains the best short this lab has. Champion unchanged.

name: WF v11 bidirectional, 6h picks the side
description: One bidirectional cascade per the user's design: the 6h regime decides the side, long on 4+ green HA 1h candles and short on 2 or fewer, with the same 15m sweep-and-reverse mechanics either way. E13's 3m cycle-position gate applies to the SHORT side only, as the location fix the long gets for free. Both legs reported separately.
notes: THE STRUCTURE THE USER ASKED FOR NOW EXISTS, AND THE SHORT LEG DRAGS. PF 1.5689 against the champion's 1.6862 and DD 3.382% against 3.103%, so it loses on BOTH ratchet terms and the champion is unchanged. THE SPLIT IS THE POINT: longs 32 trades, 18 wins, +$786.08 -- identical count to the champion, so the long side is untouched. Shorts 6 trades, 1 win, -$65.03. The entire shortfall is the short leg, and six trades in 4.6 months means the bear regime plus the cycle gate is far too restrictive to contribute anything. This is the first War Formation build that is bidirectional by construction rather than long-only, so it becomes the base for that work even though it does not beat the champion. The next question is frequency on the short side, not quality: with six trades there is nothing to judge.

name: WF v12 bidirectional, greenBear 3
description: v11 bidirectional with one change: the bear regime loosened from 2 or fewer green HA 1h candles to 3 or fewer, to raise short-leg frequency above v11's six trades. Long side untouched. Both legs reported separately.
notes: MORE SHORTS, SAME SINGLE WINNER, FIVE TIMES THE LOSS. Shorts went 6 to 10 while wins stayed at 1, and the short leg's loss grew from -$65.03 to -$328.77. Combined PF fell 1.5689 to 1.3026 and drawdown rose 3.382% to 5.021%. The long leg is untouched at 32 trades with 18 wins and +$785.70, which confirms the change was isolated to the bear regime as intended. THE SHORT LEG IS NOT MERELY RARE, IT IS BAD: one winner in ten. Loosening frequency does not help a leg with no edge, it just samples the same negative expectancy more often -- which is the honest answer to the frequency question raised by v11. Champion unchanged.

name: WF E28 short leg + the coil
description: E13's exact recovered source with exactly one addition: the 3m coil (atr3 < atr30 * 0.85) read on the prior bar. Recovering E13 showed its short has never had the volatility-contraction gate the long has required since v1. Not a mirror -- a component the long has always had and the short was never given. Short-only, judged alone.
notes: THE COIL REMOVED THE GOOD SHORTS. E13 0.74897196 on 39 trades -> 0.49037037 on 17. The gate cut 22 of 39 trades and profit factor fell by a third, so what it removed was disproportionately the winners. This is E14 in mirror image: there the weakening gate removed good longs because it duplicated the coil; here the coil itself removes good shorts. The contraction that precedes a long reclaim is not the state that precedes a short break -- the long waits for stillness before a spring, the short needs the move already going. Ninth short construction, still no PF above 1.0. REVERTED.

name: WF E29 breakdown continuation short
description: The first short in this lab that does not enter at a level. Bear regime, a genuine break of the previous 15m low, a momentum trigger extending the break, stop above the previous 15m high. Deliberately no coil (E28 measured it removing winners) and no cycle-position gate (it exists to prevent shorting after a fall, which this design does on purpose). Short-only.
notes: CONTINUATION IS WORSE THAN REVERSAL, AND IT IS NOT CLOSE. PF 0.5549 against E13's 0.7490, on 336 trades versus 39 -- the largest short sample this lab has ever produced, so the verdict is not a sample-size question. Removing the level requirement multiplied frequency 8.6x and made every trade worse. Tenth short construction, still nothing above 1.0. The level was never the problem. REVERTED.

name: WF E30 champion ported to 5m
description: The champion ported to 5m to obtain a 2.2-year sample instead of 4.5 months, because the time-concentration finding rests on only 32 trades. v6 reconstructed from pine/war-formation-v8-weakening.pine, which contains its baseSig verbatim. maxBars 720 to 144; the atr(3)/atr(30) coil cannot be scaled below one bar and is kept, declared. Long-only. TWO variables move at once -- timeframe and period -- which is a deliberate and disclosed tradeoff for sample size.
notes: THE CHAMPION DOES NOT SURVIVE A LONGER SAMPLE. PF 1.68623784 on 32 trades in 4.5 months at 1m becomes PF 0.3288793 on 38 trades across 2.2 years at 5m. The payoff ratio collapses from the champion's profile to 1.06 and the win rate falls to 23.7%. TWO CAVEATS, both mine: the run confounds timeframe with period, and the v6 reconstruction is unverified. Neither rescues the result -- a mechanism with a real edge should not invert this hard -- but they do mean the missing control (5m on the 1m window) must run before this is called decisive. REVERTED; champion unchanged.

name: WF E31 5m port on the 1m window (control)
description: The missing control for E30, which moved timeframe and period at once. Byte-identical Pine to E30, run on the champion's own window, so the only difference from v6 is the timeframe. Long-only.
notes: THE COLLAPSE IS THE TIMEFRAME, NOT THE PERIOD -- AND THIS CORRECTS E30's WRITTEN CONCLUSION. On the champion's own window the 5m port scores PF 0.39362758 on 9 trades against v6's 1.68623784 on 32. E30 (2.2 years) scored 0.32887930 and E31 (4.5 months) scores 0.39362758: essentially the same number on wildly different periods, so period explains nothing and timeframe explains everything. Trade frequency falls 32 to 9 on an identical window, which means the 1m trigger simply does not survive aggregation to 5m. CONSEQUENCE: E30 did NOT test whether the champion holds up on a longer sample, and my conclusion there that PF 1.686 was probably a small-sample artifact was an overreach. That question is still open, and the 5m route to answering it is now closed.

name: WF 950-1 population counter (diagnostic)
description: A COUNTER, NOT A STRATEGY. Step one of the user-supplied 950 Rule queue: measure the population before building. Long entries fire on each 950 signal (price within 50 of a whole thousand, both directions), short entries on each take of that whole number, one-bar exits. So longTrades is the signal count, shortTrades the take count, and their ratio is the hit rate. P&L meaningless by construction.
notes: THE POPULATION IS LARGE; THE HIT RATE IS A COIN FLIP. 3,097 signals produced 1,589 takes within 24 hours -- 51.3%. The rule states the whole number WILL be taken. Measured at a tradeable horizon it is 51%. TWO CAVEATS, BOTH MINE AND BOTH REAL: (1) the rule says time does not matter and I imposed a 1,440-bar expiry, so this tests the rule AT A HORIZON, not as stated; with no expiry the rate would approach 100% but would not be tradeable with a fixed stop. (2) an armed level blocks re-arming until it resolves or expires, so a stale arm can suppress later signals -- this depresses both counts and the ratio is the robust output. Frequency is not the problem here; certainty is.

name: WF 950-2 velocity split counter (diagnostic)
description: A COUNTER, NOT A STRATEGY. Step two of the 950 Rule queue: define velocity numerically and measure whether it discriminates. STRONG = body at least 0.60 of candle range AND range at least 1.0x atr(30); WEAK is everything else. Long entries fire on strong takes, short entries on weak takes, so longTrades/shortTrades is the split. Also fixes 950-1's stale-arm defect. P&L meaningless by construction.
notes: THE VELOCITY LABEL DISCRIMINATES: 2,347 strong (48.3%) against 2,517 weak (51.7%) out of 4,864 takes. Balanced, so it is a usable discriminator rather than a label that tags everything one way -- step 2 passes. BUT IT ALSO INVALIDATES 950-1's HIT RATE. The stale-arm fix took the take count from 1,589 to 4,864, which is more than 950-1 counted as SIGNALS, so that run's 51.3% was computed on a broken arm counter and must not be quoted. The hit-rate question is reopened and needs a clean re-run. What survives from 950-1 is only that the population is large.

name: WF 950-1b signal counter (diagnostic)
description: A COUNTER, NOT A STRATEGY. Re-counts the 950 signals with the arming logic fixed in 950-2, restoring the number 950-1 got wrong. Arms only -- longs are upward signals, shorts downward -- so arms never compete with takes for the position slot. Takes come from 950-2, measured with identical arming. P&L meaningless by construction.
notes: THE RULE'S PREMISE IS VINDICATED AND MY COIN-FLIP CLAIM WAS WRONG. 5,119 signals (2,576 up, 2,543 down) against 4,864 takes from 950-2 = a 95.0% hit rate within 24 hours, not 51.3%. The user's rule says the whole number WILL be taken and at this horizon it essentially is. BUT THE INFORMATION CONTENT IS LOW AND THAT MATTERS MORE: the signal fires when price is already within $50 of the level, and on 1m BTC a $50 move inside 24 hours is close to free. A near-certain prediction of a nearly-certain event is not an edge. The rule's value has to come from step 3, the velocity read, which 950-2 showed splits 48/52 and is therefore a real discriminator.

name: WF 950-3 strong-break continuation
description: The first real strategy built from the user's 950 Rule, and the test of its load-bearing claim: does the velocity label predict? Continuation leg only -- a STRONG break of a whole number is followed toward the next one, longs on upward breaks and shorts on downward, so the legs split cleanly by direction. Target is the next whole number and the stop is the 60-bar swing, both from the rule's own geography rather than an invented R multiple.
notes: STRONG BREAKS DO NOT CONTINUE. PF 0.60548046 on 606 trades. Longs 338 (142W, 42.01% win, -$3,996.05); shorts 268 (52W, 19.40% win, -$2,879.84). Both legs lose and neither is close. The velocity label DISCRIMINATES -- 950-2 measured a 48/52 split -- but on the continuation half it does not PREDICT. Note the asymmetry: upward strong breaks win 42.0% against 19.4% for downward, so the long side of this rule is far healthier than the short even though both lose, which matches every other result in these labs. This kills the continuation claim only; the weak-break fade is a separate claim and is untested. REVERTED.

name: WF 950-4 weak-break fade
description: The last untested claim in the user's 950 Rule, and the half the infographic emphasises most. A WEAK break of a whole number is faded back toward the previous one: shorts on weak upward breaks, longs on weak downward breaks, so the legs split by direction and each is judged alone. Same geography as 950-3, opposite prescription.
notes: THE FADE BEATS THE CONTINUATION AND STILL LOSES. PF 0.73240142 on 533 trades against 950-3's 0.60548046 on 606. Shorts 250 (38W, 15.20% win, -$3,142.77); longs 283 (117W, 41.34% win, -$1,741.49). So the velocity label does carry SOME directional information -- fading a weak break is meaningfully better than following a strong one -- but neither prescription clears 1.0. THE LONG/SHORT ASYMMETRY REPEATS EXACTLY: 41.34% versus 15.20% here, 42.01% versus 19.40% in 950-3. Twelfth short construction in this project; best remains E13 at 0.74897196, which this does not beat. REVERTED.

name: WF E32 no coil (signal-term binding test)
description: HARD LESSON 15 applied to this lab: the binding test on a SIGNAL term rather than a filter. One change from v6: coilPrev removed -- the 3m volatility contraction, the mechanisation of the Oracle's central observation, present in every build since v1 and never once removed from the long side. E14 checked in advance: nothing else in the conjunction measures volatility contraction.
notes: THE COIL IS THE MOST LOAD-BEARING TERM IN THE CHAMPION, AND THIS IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF BTC's ATTACK 15. Removing it takes trades 32 to 67 and profit factor 1.68623784 to 0.61133755, with the win rate collapsing 56.25% to 35.82%. So it removes 35 of 67 candidates and they are overwhelmingly losers. Where BTC's named term was decoration that cost money, this lab's named term IS the edge. The reconstruction is also validated in the only direction it can be: removing a term can only ADD trades, and 67 > 32 is consistent. REVERTED; champion unchanged.
